WITNESSETH: WHEREAS, pursuant to that certain Ground Lease Agreement dated of an even date herewith (the “Ground Lease”), by and between The University of Rhode Island, a public institution of higher education established by the laws of the State of Rhode Island, for itself and on behalf of its governing board, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, a public corporation created and established pursuant to Chapter 32, Title 16 of the General Laws of Rhode Island (together referred to as the “University”), as lessor, and Lessee, as lessee, the University has leased certain Property (as defined in the Ground Lease, “Property”) to Lessee.

WHEREAS, pursuant to the terms of the Ground Lease, Lessee will design, develop, finance, construct, furnish, equip, operate, manage and maintain two (2) new on- campus undergraduate student housing communities (the “New Undergraduate Housing Projects”) and will demolish, design. develop, finance, construct, furnish, equip, operate, manage and maintain one (1) on-campus graduate student and family housing community (the “Graduate Housing Project” and collectively, with the Undergraduate Housing Projects, the “Student Housing Facilities” and each, a “Student Housing Facility”) to serve each and every Resident, pursuant to the terms of the Ground Lease.

One of the Undergraduate Housing Projects to be known as “Flagg Hall” (“Student Housing Facility 1”) will be an approximately 135,177 gross square foot apartment-style building with 95 four-bedroom single occupancy units and approximately 400 student beds located on Site 1 (as defined in the Ground Lease) ; and the other Undergraduate Housing Project to be known as “ North Gateway Hall ” (“Student Housing Facility 2 ”) will be an approximately 173,739 gross square foot apartment -style building with 123 four-bedroom single occupancy units and approximately 514 student beds located on Site 2 (as defined in the Ground Lease).
The Graduate Housing Project (“Student Housing Facility 3”) will be comprised of a mix of studio, one-bed, two-bed and three- bed apartment style units in one or more buildings with 160 units and approximately 220 student beds located on Site 3 (as defined in the Ground Lease).

The Student Housing Facilities will include all Personalty (as defined in the Ground Lease ), amenities and improvements required for or in connection with the use, occupancy, lease and operation of the Student Housing Facilities , including, without limitation, utilities, driveways, approaches, sidewalks, parking lots, landscaping, lighting, security systems, other site improvements, exterior and interior improvements made a part of the Student Housing Facilities as set forth in the final construction drawings and plans and specifications to be approved by the Parties for the Student Housing Facilities.
WHEREAS, each of the Student Housing Facilities will be constructed at different times.

2 4923-6384-1828.6 WHEREAS, under the Ground Lease, the Lessee has the right and obligation to engage a Manager to manage the day -to-day operation, management, maintenance, and repair of the Student Housing Facilities.
WHEREAS, the sole member of Lessee is Provident Resources Group Inc., a Georgia nonprofit corporation and a qualified tax- exempt charitable organization under §501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code (the “ Lessee Parent ”) whose charitable purposes include, but are not limited to, the advancement of education and the lessening of burdens of government, and in furtherance thereof, the acquisition, design, construction, development, ownership, improvement, operation, management, lease, sale, conveyance, mortgage, encumbrance, financing and refinancing of student housing, e ducational facilities, administrative facilities and community public facilities used by and for the benefit of government entities, schools, colleges and universities and other organizations that qualify as exempt from taxation pursuant to Section 501(c)(3) of the Code .

WHEREAS, the Lessee is organized exclusively to further the stated charitable purposes of Lessee Parent and, specifically, for the purpose of owning, using, operating, maintaining, supporting and/or improving the Student Housing Facilities and providing certain student housing services for the University, exclusively for the benefit and support of the University and its students and assisting or otherwise supporting the educational mission of the University; WHEREAS, the Lessee desires to engage the Manager as the Manager of the Student Housing Facilities, and the Manager desires to accept such engagement from the Lessee, for the Term and upon the terms and conditions that are set forth herein.
WHEREAS, the Parties intend for this Agreement to be a “qualified management contract” that complies with the safe harbor conditions under IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-13 under which a management contract does not result in private business use of property financed with governmental tax -exempt bonds under §141(b) of the Internal Revenue Code or cause the modified private business use test for property financed with qualified 501(c)(3) bonds under § 145(a)(2)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code to be met.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises hereinafter set forth and of other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: ARTICLE I ROLE OF MANAGER Section 1.1 Appointment and Acceptance.
The Lessee hereby engages the Manager as an independent contractor to handle the day- to-day management, operation, maintenance, and repair of the Student Housing Facilities, and Manager accepts such engagement, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement and in the Ground Lease and subject to the obligations set forth in the Responsibility Matrix attached to this Agreement as Exhibit B ; provided, however, notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Manager shall not have any responsibility for those items which are the responsibility of the University or Lessee as set forth in the Responsibility Matrix.

In the event that any responsibility related directly to the management, operation, maintenance, repair and replacement of the Project under the Ground Le ase is not specifically addressed in this Agreement, the same shall be the responsibility of the Manager using its best efforts if such responsibility is designated as a responsibility of the Manager under the Responsibility Matrix; provided that should any management, operation, maintenance, repair and replacement responsibilities assumed by the Manager pursuant to this sentence materially increase the Manager’s performance or payment obligations under this Agreement, Lessee shall

3 4923-6384-1828.6 in good faith work with t he Manager to address such material increases in the Annual Budget and shall consider and approve, in Lessee’s reasonable discretion, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, a corresponding adjustment to the Annual Budget to reflect such material increases.
The Lessee and Manager will cooperate with the personnel of the University in connection with the management and operation of the Student Housing Facilities .
The Lessee hereby grants to the Manager all power and authority to do and perform any and every act and thing whatsoever requisite, necessary, or proper to be done in the exercise of any of the rights or powers herein granted, and Manager hereby agrees to do and perform any and every act and thing whatsoever requisite, necessary or proper to be done by the Manager under this Agreement.

Nothing contained in this Agreement shall obligate Manager to itself incur any monetary liability or obligation in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement, and, except as otherwise set forth herein, any monetary expenses, liabilities or obligations incurred by Manager in the performance of its obligations hereunder shall be Program Expenses (as defined below).
Section 1.2 Operational Standards .

The Manager shall operate the Student Housing Facilities, unless such operations are not the responsibility of the Manager under the Responsibility Matrix or this Agreement: (a) in accordance with all Applicable Laws; (b) in a manner consistent with the standards of practice followed by professional managers of other privately operated on-campus housing projects of a size, class and nature comparable to the size, class and nature of the Student Housing Facilities; and (c) in compliance with all University Policies provided: (i) such policies that are enforced on a Campus -wide basis and are not applied or enforced in a manner that discriminates or results in prejudice to the Lessee or the Manager, (ii) such policies have officially been adopted by the University and written notice of such policies have been provided to the Manager, (iii) the University and Lessee have approved an adjustment to the Annual Budget, if reasonably necessary for such compliance and/or any expenses incurred for such compliance will be within the Annual Budget ; and (iv) such compliance will not have any effect on the background check of employees of the Manager, which background checks will be based solely on internal policies of the Manager.

The Manager shall at all times act in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner to protect and to account for the assets of the University and the Lessee.
The Manager shall not have any responsibility for enforcing (a) the University’s Community Standards and Student Conduct system with respect to any Student Housing Facilities or (b) any Housing Agreement with respect to the New Undergraduate Housing Projects, but may need to reflect any policy changes thereunder in the Annual Budget.
The Manager shall, and shall cause its employees to, use reasonable good faith efforts to report to the University any suspected violations of the Student Code of Conduct.
Section 1.3 Transaction Documents.
This Agreement is subject to the terms and conditions of the following documents (collectively, the “Transaction Documents”), so long as such documents are still in effect: (a) this Agreement, (b) the Ground Lease, (c) the Development Agreement, (d) the Affiliation Agreement, and (e) the Bond Documents, and any exhibits to such documents, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time.

The Manager shall not take any action that is inconsistent with, constitutes a default under, or exceeds the scope of the Lessee’s or the Manager’s authority under, the Transaction Documents, and shall not omit to take any action required under the Transaction Documents that falls within the scope of the Manager’s responsibility under this Agreement.
In the event of any conflict between the express terms and conditions of this Agreement and the terms and conditions of the Transaction Documents, the terms and conditions of the Transaction Documents shall govern and prevail.
ARTICLE II MARKETING AND LEASING RESPONSIBILITIES Section 2.1 Generally.
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Manager shall not have any marketing responsibilities with respect to the N ew Undergraduate Housing Projects unless otherwise provided in the Responsibility Matrix.
In accordance with Section 16.2 of the Ground Lease, the Manager (on behalf of Lessee) shall, without the consent or approval of the University,

4 4923-6384-1828.6 have the right in the ordinary course of business, to enter into Housing Agreements with Residents of the Graduate Housing Project pursuant to one or more forms of Housing Agreements which forms shall be subject to the reasonable approval of the University .
Except as otherwise provided in the Responsibility Matrix, the Manager shall be responsible for (i) marketing and promoting the Graduate Housing Project to the extent provided on the Responsibility Matrix, (ii) coordinating the move-in and move-out of Residents within the Graduate Housing Project ; and (iii) providing those services which are the obligation of the Manager under the Responsibility Matrix; provided, however, with respect to providing such services under this item (iii), any costs for such services shall be a Program Expense.
The Manager shall be responsible for maintenance and operation duties under the Housing Agreements and for any supplemental marketing of the Graduate Housing Project to prospective Residents of the Graduate Housing Project, all in accordance with the terms of this Agreement.

The Manager shall not have any responsibility for Residence Life Programs, if any , at the New Undergraduate Housing Projects.
None of the Manager, Lessee or the University intend to engage hall directors, resident assistants or community assistants to be assigned to the Graduate Housing Project.
Section 2.2 Marketing.
Except as otherwise provide d in, and subject to, the Responsibility Matrix, t he Manager shall be primarily responsible for evaluating the need for any marketing and promotional activities for the Graduate Housing Project, and shall prepare and implement marketing campaigns, materials, copy, and promotional activities to promote and increase Resident demand or other market demand for the Graduate Housing Project.
As a part of the Manager’s marketing efforts, any tours of the Graduate Housing Project shall be conducted or coordinated by the Manager.
The Manager shall include the cost of any marketing efforts in the Annual Budget, and any such marketing costs shall be Program Expenses.

The Manager shall obtain approval of the University and follow the University’s policies and procedures when incorporating the colors, logos and branding of the University in its printed and electronic advertising materials, and shall exert reasonable efforts to integrate the Manager’s marketing efforts with the University’s branding and marketing efforts for the University or on -campus living as a whole.
Section 2.3 Website Operation .
The Manager shall have the Graduate Housing Project represented and marketed on the Manager’s and University’s websites, which will allow applications for housing to be completed and filed and provide a URL address for students and other potential Residents to access the Manager's work order system.
The Manager will have a separate website for these purposes.
The Manager’s website shall include a mechanism for filing an Application for residency within the Graduate Housing Project and the Manager shall work with the University to establish a link between the University and the Manager’s website, through which an Application may be filed.
Applications may also be filed through Manager via mail or in person.

Section 2.4 Management of Occupancy Rates and Demand .
The Manager shall exert commercially reasonable efforts consistent with its scope of authority under this Agreement and the requirements of the Transaction Documents to maximize the occupancy of the Graduate Housing Project in a fiscally sustainable manner.
In connection therewith, the Manager shall review and analyze the application of any University Policies by the University in connection therewith, and shall review and analyze the potential impact of any change of such University Policies by the University.
In either case, the Manager shall advise the Lessee as to whether or not the University Policies may violate the Ground Lease or result in an adverse impact on student occupancy of the Graduate Housing Project.
Section 2.5 Resident Application and Selection Procedures.

With respect to Residents of the Graduate Housing Project, the Manager will manage and administer the housing application and lease up process for the Graduate Housing Project during the Term, including, without limitation, the procedures for accepting housing applications from Applicants, selecting Residents for the Graduate Housing Project, making room assignments within the Graduate Housing Project, and facilitating student transfers between

5 4923-6384-1828.6 the Graduate Housing Project and any other housing on Campus.
The Manager may charge an Application Fee to Residents of the Graduate Housing Project, as reasonably determined by Manager.
Section 2.6 Termination of Housing Agreements.
The Manager, on behalf of the Lessee, shall permit any Resident of the Graduate Housing Project to terminate his or her Housing Agreement pursuant to the terms of such Housing Agreement or otherwise required by the Transaction Documents.
The Manager shall decide, based on the terms and conditions of the Housing Agreement and in consultation with the Lessee, when to terminate a Housing Agreement of any Resident of the Graduate Housing Project who materially violates University Policies or the terms of the Housing Agreement.
In the event that any Housing Agreement with respect to the Graduate Housing Project is terminated early, the Manager shall administer and manage the process of providing refunds to Residents (if applicable), the assessment of resident housing termination fees, and shall manage and supervise the physical move -out of the Resident from the Graduate Housing Project in which the Resident is residing .

The Manager shall be responsible for any eviction proceedings of a Resident from the Graduate Housing Project and any costs related thereto shall be Program Expenses.
Section 2.7 Move-In and Move-Out.
With respect to the Residents of the Graduate Housing Project, t he Manager shall coordinate and implement Resident move -in and move -out logistics, to disseminate information to Residents about the move-in and move-out process, and to provide maintenance availability during all Resident move -in and Resident move -out periods; provided, however, that Lessee shall cause the University to provide all custodial availability during all Resident move -in and Resident move-out periods for all New Undergraduate Housing Projects.
Section 2.8 Room Assignments and Tran sfers.
The Manager shall be responsible for assigning each Resident of the Graduate Housing Project to a particular unit within the Graduate Housing Project based on selected preferences by such Resident, if any of the Graduate Housing Project , and as available.
Section 2.9 Attornment.

Manager shall ensure that all Housing Agreements for the Graduate Housing Project include an attornment clause providing in effect that in the event of a change in ownership of the Graduate Housing Project, each Resident under a Housing Agreement for such Graduate Housing Project agrees, at the election and upon demand of any owner of such Graduate Housing Project, to attorn, from time to time, to any such owner upon the terms and conditions set forth in the Housing Agreement and further, that at the request of the party to whom it has attorned, it will execute, acknowledge, and deliver, without charge, from time to time, instruments acknowledging such attornment.

The attornment clause shall also provide that upon such attornment, the Housing Agreement for the Graduate Housing Project shall continue in full force and effect as, or as if it were, a direct residency agreement between the successor and the Resident under such Housing Agreement, except that the successor landlord shall not (i) have any liability for any previous act or omission of a predecessor landlord under the Housing Agreement, (ii) be bound by any previous modification of the Housing Agreement, unless such modification shall have been expressly approved in writing as contemplated in the Bond Documents, or (iii) have any liability for refusal or failure to perform or complete the predecessor landlord’s work or otherwise prepare such Graduate Housing Project for occupancy in accordance with the provisions of the Housing Agreement.
Section 2.10 Parking.
Manager will have no responsibility with respect to providing parking for the Residents.
Section 2.11 Furniture Fixtures and Equipment .

With respect to the replacement of any furniture, fixtures or equipment in the Student Housing Facilities which have become defective, worn -out or obsolete after the Effective Date, the Manager shall be responsible for the selection, design and installation of all furniture, fixtures and equipment to replace such defective, worn-out or obsolete furniture,

6 4923-6384-1828.6 fixtures or equipment, subject to the approval of the Lessee and the University and provided the costs related thereto are within the Annual Budget at the time of such replacement .
The responsibilities for moving of furniture each summer shall be per the Responsibility Matrix.
ARTICLE III MAINTENANCE AND REPAIR RESPONSIBILITIES Section 3.1 Generally.
Except as otherwise provided in the Responsibility Matrix, t he Manager shall maintain and repair the Student Housing Facilities, and all constituent elements and systems thereof, in good working order and condition, in accordance with all Applicable Laws, University Policies and the Transaction Documents, and otherwise in a condition at all times reasonably acceptable to the Lessee; provided the expenses related thereto are within the Annual Budget .

Except for the procurement of janitorial and custodial supplies for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects , which shall be the responsibility of the University, the Manager is authorized to purc hase all materials , equipment, tools, appliances, supplies and services necessary to assure proper maintenance and repair of the Student Housing Facilities subject to the limits of the Annual Budget, and all of such costs shall be Program Expenses.
The Manager’s maintenance and repair obligations shall include, but are not limited to, maintenance and operation of the HVAC equipment, elevator systems, and other mechanical equipment and operation systems serving the Student Housing Facilities, and all other necessary maintenance of and repairs to the Student Housing Facilities to the extent funds are made available pursuant to the Annual Budget; provided, however, the Manager shall not be responsible for any custodial services at the New Under graduate Housing Projects.
Lessee shall cause the University to be responsible for all landscaping and snow removal of the Student Housing Facilities.

The Manager shall not be responsible for any landscaping of the Student Housing Facilities, but will cause the University to be reimbursed as a Program Expense for any expenses incurred by the University for such landscaping , provided such expenses are within the Annual Budget .
The Manager shall not be responsible for any snow removal of the Student Housing Facilities, but will cause the University to be reimbursed as a Program Expense for any expenses incurred by the University for such snow removal from the areas between the line that is twenty feet from the exterior doors of the Student Housing Facilities to the adjacent parking areas, as more particularly detailed in the Affiliation Agreement and the Responsibility Matrix, provided such expenses are with in the Annual Budget.
The Manager shall not have any responsibility for the maintenance of any exterior signs adjacent to any of the Student Housing Facilities, but will maintain signs affixed to the Student Housing Facilities, subject to the approval of the University, provided all costs incurred for such maintenance of signs affixed to the Student Housing Facilities is a Program Expense and is reflected in the Annual Budget.

The Manager shall not have any responsibility for the maintenance, lighting, snow removal or cleaning of any parking lots and the costs thereof shall not be a Program Expense.
Section 3.2 Work Order Management.
The Manager shall track and document work orders using an electronic system to manage work orders that is selected and implemented by the Manager, or with the consent of the Lessee, implemented by the Lessee.
Information gathered through the use of the wo rk order system will be used to assist in monitoring and maintaining the Student Housing Facilities, and the work order system will assist the Manager in tracking preventative maintenance and annual inspections to determine the condition of the Student Housing Facilities.
The work order system shall have an online user interface that will allow online submission of requests by Residents and residence life staff, provide notifications of work orders to the Manager, and provide the Lessee and the University with access to status reports and dashboards.
The work order system shall also track the amount of time occurring between work order submission and work order completion.

Provided work order completion for any work order submission has not occurred within a reasonable amount of time after such work order submission and after at least t hirty (30) days advance written notice by the University to the Manager and the Lessee of such failure to complete in a reasonable amount of time, the University or the Lessee may complete the work in such work order submission; provided, however, if the work in such work order submission has commenced

7 4923-6384-1828.6 within such thirty (30) day period and is proceeding in a reasonable manner, then the University and the Lessee shall not have the right to complete such work.
Section 3.3 Use of Maintenance Employees.
The Manager will utilize the services of its regular maintenance employees to maintain and repair the Student Housing Facilities except in circumstances where the Manager determines that use of such employees for a given task would be an unproductive use of their time, where the Manager determines that the use of a third party vendor or contractor would likely yield superior results than the use of its regular employees, or when such employees are otherwise occupied or unavailable; provided, however, the use of such third party vendors or contractors shall not increase the expenses set forth in Annual Budget without Lessee’s approval (and the approval of the University, if required by the Ground Lease).
Section 3.4 Preventative Maintenance.

The Manager shall develop and implement preventative maintenance and scheduled service plans (“Preventative Maintenance Plans”) for all capital equipment of the Student Housing Facilities, which Preventative Maintenance Plans shall be presented to and subject to the approval of, the University as part of the process of determining the Annual Budget each Annual Period.
The Manager shall schedule and perform preventative maintenance on the Student Housing Facilities consistent with good maintenance and repair practices, and in accordance with the Preventative Maintenance Plan, subject to limitations contained in the Annual Budget.
Section 3.5 Damage by Residents The Manager shall assess and determine any and all damages to a Student Housing Facility beyond reasonable wear and tear caused by any Resident or such Resident’s guests.

Based on such assessment and determination of damages by the Manager, t he Lessee shall cause the University to invoice any such Resident in a New Undergraduate Housing Project and the Manager will invoice any such Resident in the Graduate Housing Project for the costs to repair any such damage for which such Resident is responsible in accordance with a damages and billing sheet, the form of which has been mutually agreed upon by the Manager, Lessee and University.
Section 3.6 Capital Improvements and Work .
The Lessee, and not the Manager, will be primarily responsible for causing the completion of the construction of the Student Housing Facilities pursuant to the Development Agreement.
With respect to each Student Housing Facility, i f Lessee is permitted, pursuant to Section 13.2 of the Ground Lease, to make additional capital improvements to the Property applicable to such Student Housing Facility after the Effective Date for such Student Housing Facility, the Manager shall include all such planned capital improvements in its proposed Annual Budget.

The Manager shall develop a capital im provement plan for the first ten (10) years of the Term detailing capital improvements that will be needed to the Student Housing Facilities during such period of time (“Capital Improvement Plan”), which Capital Improvement Plan shall be presented to and s ubject to the approval of the University as part of the process of determining the Annual Budget each Annual Period.
The Manager, consistent with the Capital Improvement Plan shall be responsible for planning, designing, managing, implementing and constructing major and minor capital improvements at the Student Housing Facilities and/or supervising third -party construction agents responsible for managing any such capital improvements at the Student Housing Facilities .

In connection with such work, the Manager shall be responsible for (a) preparing and reviewing all draw requests for submission to the Lessee and, if requested by Lessee, pay all draw requests on approval by Lessee; (b) requiring each contractor and subcontractor to maintain insurance as required by the Transaction Documents or such greater coverages as are required by the Lessee; and (c) soliciting competitive bids from such contractors when required by Applicable Law or when the cost of a capital improvement exceeds $50,000.
Prior to undertaking any work or responsibilities which Manager believes are not already obligations of the Manager pursuant to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Manager shall submit to Lessee a proposal with sufficien t detail that outlines such additional work or responsibilities, why the Manager believes such additional work or responsibilities are not contemplated by this Agreement, the anticipated labor and overhead costs to be incurred by the Manager

8 4923-6384-1828.6 in order to pe rform such additional work or responsibilities, and any additional fees or charges proposed for such work (such costs, fees and charges, collectively the “Capital Improvement Fee ”).
If such additional work or responsibilities and the related costs are app roved by the Lessee, the Manager shall be compensated the Capital Improvement Fee for such additional work or responsibilities (as a Program Expense), which shall be in addition to the Base Management Fee and Property Management Performance Incentive Fee.
Section 3.7 Ownership of Personal Property .
The Lessee shall own all Personalty located in the Student Housing Facilities as of the Effective Date, other than property of Residents or other third parties, but the Manager, on behalf of the Lessee, has the right to use, maintain, repair, and dispose of all of such personal property in connection with the discharge of its right s and obligations hereunder.

Any such personal property and any other personal property hereinafter acquired by the Lessee, or the Manager on behalf of the Lessee, for use in connection with the Student Housing Facilities shall be conveyed to the University at the expiration or earlier termination of the Ground Lease, if so provided in the Ground Lease.
Section 3.8 Recycling and Waste Hauling.
Residents will be responsible for taking trash and items to be recycled from their units to designated trash areas for the Student Housing Facilities containing separate trash and recycling bins.
The Lessee will cause the University to remove trash and items to be recycled in the common areas of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to such designated trash areas for the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and the Manager will remove trash and items to be recycled in the common areas of the Graduate Housing Project to such designated trash areas for the Graduate Housing Project.

The Lessee will cause the University to arrange for the pickup of such trash and recycling from all of such designated trash areas for all of the Student Housing Facilities pursuant to contracts between the University and third party contractors, which expenses shall be Program Expenses to be reflected on the Annual Budget and reimbursed to the University per the Annual Budget.
Section 3.9 Janitorial Services.
Lessee shall cause the University to provide all janitorial and custodial services to all of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and such services shall be maintained at a level of 1 to 2.9 under the APPA standards.
The Manager will provide all janitorial and custodial services for the Graduate Housing Project.
ARTICLE IV SERVICE CONTRACTS Section 4.1 Generally.

The Manager shall enter into new service contracts for the Student Housing Facilities (each, a “Service Contract,” and collectively, “Service Contracts”), in its own name or as agent and attorney- in-fact of the Lessee, in the ordinary course of its management of the Student Housing Facilities; provided, however, notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Article IV, no such Service Contracts shall be with any vendor on the University’s list of Excluded Vendor s (“Excluded Vendor”), provided such exclusion is permitted by Applicable Law.
Except in emergency situations where it is infeasible for the Manager to consult with the University’s Office of Strategic Procurement prior to engaging a vendor, Manager shall contact the University’s Office of Strategic Procurement to enquire as to the whether a potential vendor is an Excluded Vendor.
Service Contracts may govern, without limitation, the procurement of goods and services (including utilities and maintenance services) for the Student Housing Facilities and the furnishing of goods and services to Residents of the Student Housing Facilities.

All costs and expenses incurred by the Manager under the Service Contracts shall be Program Expenses.
The Manager shall keep good books and records of account relating to all Service Contracts.
The costs of any such good or service will be included and specifically identified as third party good or services in the Annual Budget.
Further, the Manager covenants that (i) all such contracts will satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017- 13 or any successor federal guidance and (ii) no such contracts will, when taken together with this Agreement, cause this Agreement not to satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-

9 4923-6384-1828.6 13 or any successor federal guidance.
The Manager shall maintain records for pro ducts and/or services delivered to the Manager and pursuant to this Agreement for a period commencing on the Effective Date and ending the later of the date that is (i) six (6) years after expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement and (ii) the date the books and records are required to be retained under the regulations and rulings promulgated under the Internal Revenue Code.
Section 4.2 Utilities and Services.
To the extent the University has not elected to provide the services described in this Section, the Manager, on behalf of the Lessee, shall enter into Service Contracts for the provision of water, electricity, gas, and other utilities for the Student Housing Facilities , as well as pest control and extermination services for the Student Housing Facilities, utilizing such utility companies and vendors as the Manager selects in its discretion.

Electricity and any other utilities serving the Student Housing Facilities, which are provided directly or indirectly by the University or which serve more than just the Student Housing Facilities, will be sub-metered for the Student Housing Facilities.
Water usage at the Student Housing Facilities shall be sub- metered and billed to the Manager by the University, and the Manager will pay such water charges billed by the University as a Program Expense.
Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement, electricity at the Student Housing Facilities will be sub-metered and billed to the Manager and the Manager will pay such electricity charges as a Program Expense.
Section 4.3 Bidding Requirements.

Unless the Lessee shall instruct otherwise, the Manager shall use reasonable efforts to ensure that all Service Contracts for the performance of repairs or capital improvements to any Student Housing Facilit y exceeding $50,000, or f or the provision of goods and services to any Student Housing Facility exceeding $30,000, shall be awarded on the basis of a competitive bidding process managed by the Manager and approved by the Lessee; provided, however, no such Service Contract shall be awarded to an Excluded Vendor provided such exclusion is permitted by Applicable Law.
The Lessee's approval of the Annual Budget for the Student Housing Facilities shall be deemed approval for the work to be completed by Manager which is included in such Annual Budget.
Section 4.4 Term of Service Contracts.
To the extent reasonably possible under the circumstances, all Service Contracts shall contain a provision permitting Manager or Lessee to terminate them, with or without cause and without penalty or premium, with a thirty (30) day notice, or sooner if the Manager or the Lessee is no longer involved with a Student Housing Facilit y for which such Service Contract relates.

Under no circumstances shall a Service Contract exceed the Term without the consent of the Lessee.
The Lessee shall have the right to waive this requirement in its discretion.
Section 4.5 Service Contracts with Affiliates.
Subject to any restrictions contained in the Transaction Documents, the Manager shall have the right to contract with or otherwise de al with any Affiliate of the Manager for the sale of goods or services to it or to the Lessee, but only if the fees, terms and conditions for the provision of such goods or services are conspicuously disclosed in the Annual Budget and are at least as favor able to the Lessee or the Student Housing Facilities as would be obtainable in an arm’s length transaction.
The costs of any such good or service will be included and specifically identified as third party good or services in the Annual Budget.
Further, the Manager covenants that (i) all such contracts will satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-13 or any successor federal guidance and (ii) no such contracts will, when taken together with this Agreement, cause this Agreement not to satisfy the requirements of IRS Rev.
Proc. 2017-13 or any successor federal guidance.

Section 4.6 Ancillary Concessions.
Except as otherwise provided the Responsibility Matrix, the Manager shall not be responsible and the Lessee shall cause the University to be responsible for or to cause the University to retain a third party responsible for, operating, managing, repairing and replacing the laundry facilities, vending machines, the Grab and Go Deli and similar ancillary concessions located at the Student Housing Facilities during t he Term, and the costs thereof shall be the responsibility of the University and the revenues generated therefrom may be retained by the University and shall not be General

10 4923-6384-1828.6 Revenues; provided, however, the Manager shall be responsible for managing, repairing and replacing the laundry equipment at the Graduate Housing Project.
With respect to the Grab and Go Deli, the University will be charged a monthly fee for electricity based on a rate which will be the product of: i) the total electric bill for the electrical meter which measures electricity usage at the space occupied by the Grab and Go Deli plus all other space whose electricity usage is being measured by such electrical meter; and ii) the percentage of the square footage of the space occupied by the Grab and Go Deli as compared to the square footage of the total space in the Student Housing Facility that has electricity being measured by the same electrical meter.
For example, if the Grab and Go Deli is 1,000 square feet and 5,000 square feet of space in Student Housing Facility where the Grab and Go Deli is located and including the Grab and Go Deli space has electricity being measured by the same electrical meter, then the University will pay 20% of the electrical bill related to such electrical meter each month.

The Lessee shall cause the University to pay to the Manager all of such monthly fees for electricity at the Grab and Go Deli and such fees shall be included in the General Revenues.
ARTICLE V BUDGETING AND REPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES Section 5.1 Determination of Resident Housing Rates and Other Gross Fees.
The Manager, in consultation with the University, shall review and analyze market demand for the occupancy of the Student Housing Facilities and shall recommend to the Lessee the Resident Housing Rates and other Gross Fees to be charged to Residents each year.
The Lessee shall have the right to make the final decision as to the Resident Housing Rates and Gross Fees.

Section 5.2 Annual Budget. (a) The Manager, shall in consultation with Lessee and in accordance with Section 18 of the Ground Lease, develop in good faith, in its discretion and after consultation with the University , housing rates and other revenue services and a line- item operation and capital budget for the Student Housing Facilities for each Annual Period (collectively, the “Annual Budgets” and each, an “Annual Budget”) which provides for the payment of all Program Expenses and sets forth among other matters usually contained in budgets of similar nature, all information required under the Bond Documents.
Each Annual Budget shall be subject to the review and final approval of the Board of Managers.
The Annual Budget for the first Annual Period in which the Student Housing Facilities are completed has been approved by the Lessee and the University and is attached to the Ground Lease. (b) For the first Annual Period in which the Student Housing Facilities are completed, Manager shall submit a partial year budget to Lessee or the Committee, on behalf of the Lessee, no later than sixty (60) days prior to the initial occupancy of the Student Housing Facilities.

Commencing with the second Annual Period and for each Annual Period thereafter, the Manager shall submit to the Lessee or the Committee, on behalf of the Lessee, for its approval a proposed Annual Budget not later than one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the commencement of each Annual Period.
The Committee shall give Lessee notice of its approval of the Annual Budget as submitted or of its disapproval of one or more of the matters contained therein not later than thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of the first Annual Period with respect to the initial partial year and sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of such Annual Period thereafter.
If the Committee shall fail to give notice of approval or disapproval in a timely manner, then the Annual Budget as submitted to the Committee shall be deemed approved by the Committee and submitted for final approval to the Board of Managers.
In the event the Committee gives notice of its disapproval, the Committee shall promptly, in good faith, develop an Annual Budget on which the Committee can recommend to the Board of Managers for approval.
In the event Committee fails to reach agreement not later

11 4923-6384-1828.6 than thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of an Annual Period, or the Board of Managers fails to approve an Annual Budget submitted to them, the approved Annual Budget for the then current Annual Period, as increased by a factor equal to the Consumer Price Index Increase shall be implemented for the next Annual Period until a new Annual Budget is approved by Board of Managers. (c) From time to time during or in respect to an Annual Period, an Annual Budget may be modified pursuant to Section 18.3 of the Ground Lease.
The Manager may submit to Lessee proposed changes or other modifications to the Annual Budget and the Lessee shall seek in good faith to obtain such changes or modifications to the Annual Budget subject to Section 18.3 of the Ground Lease. (d) Subject to the limitations and restrictions set forth in this Agreement, the Manager, on behalf of the Lessee, shall operate the Student Housing Facilities and make expenditures in connection with the Student Housing Facilities in accordance with the Annual Budget , and shall provide quarterly budget reconciliations to Lessee.
Section 5.3 Program Expenses.

All costs paid or incurred by the Manager in connection with the exercise of its rights or the discharge of its responsibilities under this Agreement including, but not limited to, all Operating Expenses shall be Program Expenses (“ Program Expenses”); provided that Program Expenses shall not include corporate overhead costs of the Manager (including allocated costs of offsite employees) or any other cost or expenses unless such corporate overhead costs or other costs or expenses are approved in the Annual Budget.
Program Expenses shall be payable solely from the Operating Account and shall not be a personal obligation of the Manager.
Manager shall not be liable for any obligation or expenditure incurred on behalf of the Lessee if such obligation or expenditure is within the scope of Manager’s authority under this Agreement and pursuant to the Annual Budget (as the same may from time to time be amended and approved by Lessee).

Manager shall not be obligated to advance any sum of money for Lessee or the Student Housing Facilities , or lend its credit for the benefit of the Lessee or Student Housing Facilities; provided, however, if Manager elects to advance sums of money to pay for an Emergency Program Expense (as defined below) which funds are not available in the Operating Account or are not reflected in the Annual Budget, then the Annual Budget shall be amended to reflect such Emergency Program Expense and Manager shall be reimbursed for such Emergency Program Expense within thirty (30) days of Manager incurring such Emergency Program Expense.
Manager shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the actual costs of maintaining and operating the Projects shall not exceed the Annual Budget, and year to date budget variances, in excess of (i) $20,000 for any line item expense category, excluding insurance and utility costs, or (ii) 10% of the Annual Budget in the aggregate, will be explained to Lessee each month.

Except as otherwise set forth herein or except for any Emergency Program Expense, any expenditure from the Operat ing Account (i) which, with respect to any line item expense category, exceeds by $20,000 or more the amount for such line item expense category set forth in the Annual Budget, or (ii) which will cause the overall Annual Budget to be exceeded by 10% or more, shall require the approval of Lessee, which approval shall be given or denied within ten (10) days after such approval is requested.
In cases of an emergency, Manager may make expenditures for repairs or replacements without the approval of Lessee or the University, if it is necessary, in the reasonable judgment of Manager, to prevent imminent damage to property or injury to persons and such expenditures shall be a Program Expense (“Emergency Program Expense”).
Manager will promptly notify Lessee and the University of any such emergency expenditures no later than two (2) Business Days following such emergency repair or replacement, describing the cause of such emergency, the repairs or replacements undertaken in connection with such emergency, and the cost of such emergency repairs or replacements.

12 4923-6384-1828.6 Section 5.4 Reports.
Unless otherwise directed by the Lessee, the Manager shall prepare (or coordinate the preparation of) all reports that the Lessee is obligated to provide to the University or any other Person under the Transaction Documents, a preliminary list of which is attached hereto in Schedule 5.4.
The Manager shall submit drafts of all such reports to the Lessee, for the Lessee’s review and approval, before submission to any Person other than the Lessee.
All records related to the operations of the Student Housing Facilities that are under the control of the Manager, regardless of where they are housed, shall be the property of Lessee and shall be properly maintained by or under the direction of the Manager.
The Manager shall also prepare and submit to the Lessee such additional reports as are reasonably requested by Lessee on a mutually acceptable schedule, and shall furnish such information as may be requested by the Lessee from t ime to time with respect to any matter falling within the scope of the Manager’s responsibilities herein.
Section 5.5 Notice of Material Events.

The Manager will immediately notify the Lessee in the following circumstances: (a) the Manager receives any notice of any claim of violation of any Applicable Laws relating to the Student Housing Facilities , any notice of any claim of liability or for damages relating to the Student Housing Facilities, or any summons or other legal process relating to the Student Housing Facilities; (b) any actual or alleged personal injury or property damage arises at the Student Housing Facilities ; (c) circumstances arise relating to the activities of the Manager that will or may constitute a default by Lessee or any other Person under the Transaction Documents or under any Housing Agreement or Service Contract; (d) the Manager receives any information pertaining to the Lessee or the Student Housing Facilities, that requires Lessee to provide notice to the University under the Ground Lease, or that constitutes a breach by either the Lessee or the University under the Ground Lease; or (e) the Manager receives any other material information pertaining to its activities at the Student Housing Facilities.

The Manager will fully cooperate with the Lessee in all legal and arbitration proceedings relating to the Student Housing Facilities.
ARTICLE VI COLLECTIONS RESPONSIBILITIES Section 6.1 Generally.
With respect to the Graduate Housing Project, t he Manager shall use diligent efforts to demand, collect and receive (a) all Gross Fees due and payable from Residents of the Graduate Housing Project, (b) all other pass-through or bill-back charges, sums, costs or expenses of any nature whatsoever payable by third parties relating to all or any portion of the Graduate Housing Project, and (c) all other General Revenues accruing from occupancy or use of, activities at, or services provided for Residents at the Graduate Housing Project.
The Manager shall abide by the collections procedures set forth in this Section.

Until all obligations of Lessee under the Bond Documents are paid in full, all General Revenues collected by Manager in the form of cash, checks or negotiable instruments shall be promptly deposited into a “deposit only” account owned by the Lessee (the “ Manager’s Collections Account”), which General Revenues in the Manager’s Collections Account shall be swept weekly from such Manager’s Collections Account for deposit into the Revenue Fund in accordance with Section 3.3 of the Loan and Trust Agreement and then an amount equal to the greater of the following will be transferred into the Operating Account on or before the 15th day of each month, all as set forth in Section 3.3 of the Loan and Trust Agreement: (i) the amount budgeted for Program Expenses in the Annual Budget for the immediately succeeding month; and (ii) an amount equal to ten percent (10%) of the Program Expenses shown in the then current Annual Budget.
From and after the date that all obligations of Lessee under the Bond Documents are paid in full, all General Revenues collected by Manager in the form of cash, checks or negotiable instruments shall be directly deposited into the Operating Account.

All costs and expenses of the Manager incurred in connection with its collections efforts shall be Program Expenses.
Section 6.2 Collections Accounting Obligat ions.
The Manager will establish a cash management software system to identify and effectuate the transfer of General Revenues to the Manager’s

13 4923-6384-1828.6 Collections Account and maintain such system or a similar system in place for the Term to ensure that General Revenues are identified and transferred appropriately after the receipt thereof in accordance with the terms of the Transaction Documents.
With respect to the Graduate Housing Project, Manager shall reconcile occupancy by Residents of the Graduate Housing Project to the actual General Revenues from such Residents, manage the accounts receivables, and collect delinquent revenues.
The Manager shall keep accurate books and records of account tracking the sources and uses of all funds and rent rolls for Residents of the Student Housing Facilities, and shall, to the extent possible, provide electronic copies of such books and records to the Lessee and the University as reasonably requested from time to time; provided, however, Lessee shall cooperate and shall cause the University to cooperate with providing any and all information related to the sources and uses of all funds and rent rolls for Residents of the Undergraduate Housing Projects.

The Manager shall hold for a period of at least seven (7) years the Manager’s books and records that (i) evidence or relate to such General Revenues or (ii) are otherwise necessary or desirable to collect such General Revenues to the fullest extent allowed under Applicable Laws.
Section 6.3 Enforcement of Rights.
Without limitation of the foregoing and subject to the terms of the Ground Lease, the Manager shall have the right, on behalf of the Lessee and as a Program Expense, subject to the Annual Budget, to retain legal counsel to assist with the foregoing and/or to institute legal proceedings for: (a) the collection of General Revenues and other sums payable by Residents or other Persons under the terms of any of the Housing Agreements, Service Contracts, or other agreements affecting the Student Housing Facilities; (b) the ouster, eviction, removal or ejectment of Residents or other persons from the Student Housing Facilities , subject to Section 2.6 above; and (c) the enforcement of any other right, privilege, benefit, or remedy available to the Lessee pursuant to any of the Housing Agreements, the Service Contracts, or Applicable Laws.

ARTICLE VII CASH MANAGEMENT Section 7.1 Operating Account.
All funds paid to the Manager pursuant to Section 3.3(b) of the Loan and Trust Agreement, other than compensation to Manager under Article X of this Agreement, shall be promptly deposited into the Operating Account.
In addition to the Operating Account, the Manager may also use purchasing cards for miscellaneous purposes, which purchasing cards shall in no event exceed Five Thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($5,000.00).
The Manager shall maintain a ledger of Program Expenses funded from such purchasing cards.
Section 7.2 Funding the Operating Account .
The Lessee will from time to time fund the Operating Account from which the Manager shall have the right to make periodic withdrawals solely for the purpose of paying Program Expenses in accordance with the Annual Budget.
To the extent funds are available in the Operating Account, the Manager shall pay, using the funds in the Operating Account, the Program Expenses in accordance with the Annual Budget.
Section 7.3 Other Cash Management Provisions.

The Manager shall not commingle funds from the Student Housing Facilities with funds from any other project, other funds of the Manager, or funds of any other Person.
The Manager shall have no liability to the Lessee for any amounts in the Operating Account which are lost or not covered by insurance if the depository institution at which such account is maintained fails or is otherwise placed in the control of a gover nmental or quasi-governmental authority and the assets of such account are thereby forfeited in whole or in part.
The Manager shall not be obligated to make any advance to or for the account of the Lessee, or to pay any sum, except out of funds held or provided as set for in this Agreement.
The Lessee shall have the right to conduct audits of all accounts managed by the Manager, and the costs thereof shall be Program Expenses.

14 4923-6384-1828.6 ARTICLE VIII OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES OF MANAGER Section 8.1 Property Management Office.
The Manager may establish and maintain a housing management office and a maintenance office within one of the New Undergraduate Housing Projects and also within the Graduate Housing Project .
All costs of furnishing and maintaining supplies for the management and maintenance offices shall be Program Expenses.
The Lessee shall not charge and shall cause the University to not charge the Manager any rent or other usage fees for the use of the housing management and maintenance offices, but if the Universit y provides any services to such offices, such as telephone or internet access, the University shall be entitled to reimbursement therefor as Program Expenses at rates consistent with those assessed by the University to its own internal divisions and business units for similar services.

In the event the Manager becomes obligated to pay any rent, usage fees or charges for services provided to any office used by the Manager for providing property management services for the Student Housing Facilities, then such rent, usage fees or charges shall be Program Expenses to the extent included in the Annual Budget.
Section 8.2 Security and Emergency Response.
The Manager shall not have any responsibility for providing campus police or any on -site security not providing servi ces and any such services or staffing shall be the responsibility of the Lessee or the Lessee shall cause the University to provide such campus police, services or staffing.
The Manager shall coordinate with the Lessee, and the University, any responses prior to (if reasonably possible), during and after potential disasters, conflicts or emergency situations, to minimize the risk of loss of life or property.
The Manager, in collaboration with the University, shall develop a continuity of operations plan t o be utilized in the event of an emergency.
Such plan shall be reviewed and approved by the Committee annually.

Such plan will include plans for relocation of Residents for emergency or temporary housing, adequate on- call services to minimize and protect assets from actual or potential damage, and an emergency notification plan for all of the Manager’s personnel and all of the University’s personnel responsible for the same under this Agreement.
The Manager shall coordinate with the University to establi sh emergency points of contact from time to time, or pursuant to revisions and updates to the continuity of operations plan promulgated to the Manager and the University.
Manager’s point of contact (or reasonable temporary substitutions therefor) shall be available twenty -four (24) hours, seven (7) days a week.
The provision of security services and implementation of other security measures by the Manager hereunder is not guaranteed to deter criminal activity, and neither Lessee nor Manager shall be liabl e to the other or any other Person by reason of the criminal activities of any third party.
Section 8.3 Cooperation with University for Residence Life Services.

The Manager shall not be responsible for establishing, implementing, administering and/or managing various living-learning, social, educational, student conduct and crisis management activities and programs at the Student Housing Facilities (each, a “Residence Life Program”) for any of the Residents.
The Lessee and the Manager shall cooperate at all times w ith the University for the seamless and orderly performance of their respective responsibilities under the Transaction Documents to ensure the Student Housing Facilities are appropriately integrated into the Campus and to allow the University to provide a Residence Life Program for the Residents.
Section 8.4 Employment of Personnel .
Subject to the requirements of the Transaction Documents, the Manager shall hire, pay, supervise and discharge, as appropriate, all employees, contractors, subcontractors or others necessary for the performance of its obligations under this Agreement.
All such personnel shall be the employees or independent contractors of the Manager and not of the Lessee.

All matters pertaining to the employment of such employees or engagement of such independent contractors shall be the sole responsibility of the Manager, and the Lessee shall bear absolutely no responsibility or liability therefor.
The Manager shall fully comply with all Applicable Laws concerning worker’s

15 4923-6384-1828.6 compensation, social security , unemployment, tax withholding and reporting, hours of labor, wages, working conditions and all other Applicable Laws affecting or respecting the employment of such employees or the engagement of such independent contractors.
The Manager shall have no au thority to enter into any employment contract that purports to be on behalf of the Lessee, or that otherwise obligates the Lessee in any respect.
The Lessee reserves the right from time to time and at any time to require that employees or independent contractors performing any services relating to the Student Housing Facilities be subject to a satisfactory background or security check performed by the Lessee or, at the Lessee’s election, by the Manager.
All costs of such background or security checks shall be Program Expenses.
The Manager shall pay, as Program Expenses and in accordance with the Annual Budget, all costs of its employees or independent contractors performing services at or in respect to the Student Housing Facilities , including, without limitation, salaries, wages and other compensation and fringe benefits.

Such costs shall include reasonably allocated costs of those employees of the Manager who perform work related to the Student Housing Facilities but who are not devoted full-time to the Student Housing Facilities.
The Manager shall not be responsible for hiring staff for the front desk at any of the Student Housing Facilities.
Section 8.5 Compliance with Applicable Laws.
The Manager shall take such actions as may be necessary to abide by all Applicable Laws.
The Manager shall also take such actions as may be necessary to assure full compliance by Residents with all such Applicable Laws and University Policies so long as the cost for such actions are within the Annual Budget ; provided, however , that Manager shall have no liability whatsoever for failure by Residents to comply with Applicable Laws or University Policies.

The Manager shall, with all due diligence reasonably possible under the circumstances, eliminate or discontinue any use or condition to the extent any use or condition exists at the Student Housing Facilities that violates any Applicable Laws or University Policies or that void or would void any policy of insurance covering the Student Housing Facilities or render any loss incapable of collection thereunder.
Unless otherwise directed by the Lessee, the Manager shall have the right to contest any alleged violation of Applicable Laws and to postpone compliance pending the determination of such contest, provided such postponed compliance does not subject the Lessee, the Manager, the University or any of their respective officers, directors, trustees, agents, contractors or employees to criminal liability or subject the Student Housing Facilities or any part thereof to a lien or encumbrance as a result of such contest.
Section 8.6 Permits and Approvals.

The Manager shall be responsible for obtaining and maintaining any and all licenses, certificates, permits or approvals applicable to the Student Housing Facilities that may be required by any A pplicable Laws or University Policies to operate the Student Housing Facilities provided the expenses thereof are within the Annual Budget .
The Manager’s responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, preparing and submitting the applications and associated exhibits for such licenses, certificates, permits or approvals, and meeting with licensing personnel.
Any and all such licenses, certificates, permits or approvals shall be obtained in the name of the Lessee and/or the Student Housing Facilitie s.
Any expenses that Manager incurs in obtaining and maintaining such licenses, certificates, permits or approvals shall be Program Expenses.
Section 8.7 Tax Returns.

The Manager shall file in a timely manner all tax returns and tax forms, as applicable, for all real property, personal property, and other taxes related to the Student Housing Facilities and its operations (other than the income tax returns of the Lessee or the University ) and the Lessee shall provide to Manager and cause the University to provide to Manager all of the necessary information related to the New Undergraduate Housing Projects which are necessary for such tax returns and tax forms .
Subject to the cooperation o f the Lessee and University in providing the necessary information as provided herein, the Manager shall be responsible for the payment of all taxes related to the business of managing and operating the Student Housing Facilities , including all social secu rity, unemployment and other payroll and withholding taxes on the salaries of its own employees and agents engaged or employed at or in connection with the Student Housing Facilities, and the costs thereof shall be Program Expenses (other than the income t ax of the Manager).
The Manager will review the

16 4923-6384-1828.6 appropriateness of any and all taxes, and unless otherwise directed by the Lessee, may institute appropriate protests or challenges to the taxes and, take such other appropriate steps as it deems necessary or appropriate with respect thereto, including the retention of a property tax consultant (the costs of whom shall be Program Expenses) to assist it in determining whether to make any such challenge and the likelihood of such challenge being successful.
The Manager is not entitled to and shall not take any federal tax position that is inconsistent with being a service provider to Lessee with respect to the Student Housing Facilities .
For example, the Manager shall not take depreciation or amortization deductions, investment tax credits or deduction for payment as rent with respect to the Student Housing Facilities.
Section 8.8 Environmental Matters.

The Manager covenants, represents, and warrants to Lessee that Manager’s management of the Property shall not and will not involve the use, storage, generation, or disposal of Hazardous Materials (as defined in the Ground Lease) except in compliance with Environmental Laws, and that the Manager shall not cause or permit any Hazardous Materials to be brought, used, stored, generated, or disposed on or about the Property by the Manager, its agents, employees, contractors, subcontractors, or invitees (collectively “PM’s Parties”) except in compliance with Environmental Laws, and that with respect to its management of the Prope rty, the Manager and the PM’s Parties shall comply with all laws, including, without limitation, Environmental Laws and with all governmental authorities.
Section 8.9 Easements..
The Manager shall have no obligation to execute any easements, if any, to be executed by Lessee under the Ground Lease.
Section 8.10 Mail and Package Distribution.
The Manager shall be responsible for the mail and package distribution system for the Graduate Housing Project, but not the New Undergraduate Housing Projects.

The Manager shall maintain the current mail and package distribution system currently in place for the Graduate Housing Project.
Section 8.11 Access and Keys.
The Manager shall have access to keys for all rooms within the Graduate Housing Program to be used for maintenance, emergencies or if a Resident is locked out of their room and the Manager shall have access to keys for all rooms with in the New Undergraduate Housing Projects to be used for maintenance of the rooms.
The Manager shall not have any responsibility for Residents locked out of their rooms in the New Undergraduate Housing Projects.
All physical keys and mechanical locks are the Manager’s responsibility to manage and maintain.
The Lessee shall cause the University to be responsible for programming and issuing swipe cards or key fobs provided, however, the Manager shall be responsible for the physical upkeep of the locks (including changing batteries).
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Manager shall full access to all Student Housing Facilities for purposes of performing work orders.
Section 8.12 Customer Service.

Manager shall be responsible for customer service related to the needs of the Residents of the Graduate Housing Project and their parents (if such parent is a guarantor under a Resident Lease or such Resident is a minor).
ARTICLE IX INSURANCE AND LIABILITY Section 9.1 Insurance.
The Lessee shall have the right to source and procure the insurance coverages required to be carried by the Lessee under the Transaction Documents and any additional insurance coverages required by the Lessee; provided, however, the Manager shall have an obligation to source and procure the same if and as directed by the Lessee.
Any such insurance sourced and procured by the Lessee or the Manager (on Lessee’s behalf) shall name the Manager as an additional insured.
If the Manager sources any insurance u nder a master policy that covers additional projects managed by the

17 4923-6384-1828.6 Manager, the Manager shall provide all relevant details regarding the basis of allocating the premiums between the Student Housing Facilities and the other projects.
After insurance coverages have been procured, the Manager shall be responsible for maintaining and timely paying (or ensuring the timely payment of) all premiums for such insurance coverages provided the funds for such insurance premiums were included in the Annual Budget and such funds are available in the Operating Account.
The Manager shall review the insurance coverages of both the Lessee and the Manager on an annual basis and shall recommend any advisable changes to the Lessee and University.
Manager shall provide to Lessee and the University updated insurance certificates evidencing all required coverage at least annually.
All insurance premiums paid by the Manager on behalf of Lessee pursuant this Section or obtained by the Manager pursuant to any obligation placed on L essee pursuant to the Transaction Documents, as approved or required by the Lessee, shall be Program Expenses.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Lessee shall bear the risk of loss upon damage or destruction of the Student Housing Facilities .
Manager shall procure its own insurance as set forth on the attached Exhibit C and Lessee shall be named as an additional insured on those policies so indicated on the attached Exhibit C.
Section 9.2 Manager Indemnification.
Subject to the limitations contained in Section 9.5 below, the Manager hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Lessee and its members, managers, officers, directors, agents and employees from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, suits, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses (including court costs and reasonable legal fees) (collectively, “Claims”) asserted against or sustained by such Persons that are caused by the grossly negligent or willful acts of Manager or its agents or employees, excluding Claims caused by the gross negligence and willful misconduct of Lessee or its members, managers, officers, directors, agents or employees.
Section 9.3 Lessee Indemnification .

Subject to the limitations contained in Section 9.5 below, the Lessee hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Manager and its members, managers, officers, directors, agents and employees from and against any and all Claims asserted against or sustained by such Persons: (i) that are caused by the grossly negligent or willful acts of the Lessee or its agents or employees, excluding Claims caused by the gross negligence and willful misconduct of Manager or its members, managers, officers, directors, agents or employees; or (ii) which Claims are from an Excluded Vendor resulting from Manager not using such Excluded Vendor pursuant to Section 4.1 of this Agreement.
Section 9.4 Waiver of Subrogation.

ARTICLE X COMPENSATION OF MANAGER; COMPLIANCE WITH IRS MANAGEMENT CONTRACT GUIDELINES Section 10.1 Management Compensation.
The Manager shall be paid the following i n compensation for the performance of its duties under this Agreement: (a) A property management base fee (being a fee equal to three percent (3%) of the General Revenues in any Annual Period (“Base Management Fee”).

Such Base Management Fee will be payable in advance on or about the 20 th day of each month based on the budgeted revenues in the Annual Budget for the immediately succeeding month within the Annual Period.
Within one hundred and eighty (180) days after the end of each Annual Period, the Lessee’s accountant will prepare an audit report pursuant to the Loan and Trust Agreement (the “Audit Report”) and the General Revenues indicated by the Audit Report shall determine the actual General Revenues for such Annual Period for the purposes of thi s Agreement, and any adjustments to the Base Management Fee amounts paid for such Annual Period shall be paid or credited within thirty (30) days of Lessee’s receipt of such Audit Report. (b) Subject to the timing and payment obligations set forth in the Bond Documents, a property management performance incentive fee (being a fee not to exceed one percent ( 1%) of the General Revenues in any Annual Period) (“Property Management Performance Incentive Fee”), which shall be calculated using the Key Performance Indicator ratings that the Manager achieves for the Annual Period as listed on Exhibit D to this Agreement.

For such Annual Periods, the Property Management Performance Incentive Fee shall be payable, subject to the Bond Documents , upon certification of Lessee that, based upon the audited financial statements for such Annual Period, the Key Performance Indicator ratings have been achieved by the Manager for such Annual Period. (c) The Capital Improvement Fee and any labor and overhead costs incurred by Manager for providing any other services with respect to the Student Housing Facilities requested by the Lessee, but not otherwise required to be provided by the Manager pursuant to this Agreement.
Any such Capital Improvement Fee will be payable from the Repair and Replacement Fund established pursuant to the Loan and Trust Agreement.
In addition to the compensation described above, the Manager shall be paid as a Program Expense all of its general overhead expenses (but only to the extent the same are appr oved in the Annual Budget), payroll and general administrative expenses of any on- site employees of the Manager providing services under this Agreement and any other expenses incurred by the Manager which constitute a Program Expense and are included in the Annual Budget.

Subject to any restrictions or limitations contained in the Transaction Documents, the Manager shall be entitled to pay itself the Base Management Fee and Program Expenses payable to the Manager as and when such fees are due and payable under this Agreement or when such Program Expenses are incurred.
